title: Learned screening identifies early antiviral candidates with enzyme and cell-entry assay activity
summary: A two-stage learned screen combined SchNet molecular representations with XGBoost to prioritize compounds for laboratory evaluation. Follow-up assays identified early candidates with protease-inhibition and cell-entry activity, with additional cell and human-airway tissue-model tests. These are moderate-potency laboratory hits; direct target binding, clinical benefit and reduced resistance were not established.
ai_technology: SchNet molecular graph classification; XGBoost candidate prioritization
organization: National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences, National Institutes of Health; Texas Biomedical Research Institute; National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases

evidence.tested: The learned screen prioritized roughly 500 compounds from about 170000 library entries. The source reports 27 initial follow-up hits and examines a smaller representative subset using enzyme, cell-entry, cell-based and 3D airway-tissue assays. Four of eight detailed representatives showed moderate protease inhibition; others primarily showed entry-assay activity.
evidence.unknown: This is not evidence that every hit has a confirmed dual mechanism. Direct specific target binding remains unconfirmed; aggregation or protein-destabilization artifacts were not excluded. Some tissue-model effects coincide with cytotoxicity, and incomplete inhibition complicates potency estimates. Reduced resistance, patient efficacy and a clinical therapeutic window were not tested. The current readable journal version is represented; the publisher version-history endpoint was rate-limited, so exact timing of any later text updates is unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: SchNet learns molecular representations from prior screening measurements and filters library compounds; a second learned XGBoost layer incorporates descriptors to prioritize candidates before new laboratory measurements.

source_review.scope: Exact primary front DOI/title/date and fresh primary notice metadata; computational model/data Methods and high-level assay results/limitations read. No operational pathogen procedures represented or archived in the case evidence.
